After putting in several repeating habits I often end up in swipes that freeze on screen, it’s with both skipping and finishing habits: screen freezes and u can do nothing than restart app and it’s fixed. Till the next one freezes up.

I find this very disappointing - it looks to me the developers finished an app, and put it in the store and just sit in a beach cashing money. 
If I find this errors just after a few days into buying the app, why haven’t the developers? 

Also it has just a few icons, there’s only English, only dark mode, it’s just isn’t there yet. A bit disappointing.

title: Nice concept but have problems
body:
I like the concept of the app and the suggestions but there are things that don’t work exactly well. Changing the schedule of a habit is very annoying since it doesn’t save the first time, I’ve made it work after 3 or 4 attempts, also, this change will delete all progress you have in that habit, which is crazy. It could simply change from that day on, as a recurrent google calendar event.

I’ve noticed also, that is not possible to snooze the habit, like for example, reschedule it for another day, which could be helpful specially if updating the schedule of a habit doesn’t work properly and reset the its stats. 

The feeling I get is that there’s still work to be done to make it an stable and nice to use app, however the amount of money it costs don’t really reflect it... to make it clear, in my opinion the app cost is much higher than it should.

title: Paywalls left and right
body: It’s been said before and I know what the devs response will be, but a heads up nonetheless: you’ll not get far into this app without hitting a paywall. You can get somewhere, sure, but as soon as you want to add more than a handful of habits, boom, paywall. And that’s after a tutorial where they shove the subscription service with a limited time discount in your face multiple times a minute. It looks like a magnificent app that I’d love to use, but I’d rather pay a relatively hefty sum for an app, say a tenner or more, and have a complete experience, than have a ‘free’ app with a subscription service. Misleading gullible (read: trusting) customers is quite a toxic habit, guys...

title: Very good app with an intuitive interface.
body:
This app has been very helpful for me to track and form good daily habits, with a fun and clean layout.
Couple of suggestions for further improvement: Would like the possibility to see habits lying ahead as well as those due longer ago than one week. Would also be great to add a date/week (by) when a habit is due in a month as the beginning/middle/end function does not always work as well as it could.
